open_points.subject: A05 phase 3 endpoint validation order
open_points.text: “both ports exist with the right direction — the source an output of a node or an input of the flow, the target an input of a node or an output of the flow” does not order source existence, source direction, target existence and target direction, or say whether a port found only in the opposite direction is missing or directionally invalid
open_points.question: For one edge with multiple endpoint defects, which endpoint check and reason is the first failure, and does an opposite-direction port count as an existing port with the wrong direction or as no eligible port?
options: Validate source existence and direction atomically, then target existence and direction
Validate existence of both endpoints before checking either direction
Treat an opposite-direction port as absent and report a missing eligible source or target port
Treat an opposite-direction port as present and report a direction failure
open_points.default_guess: Validate the source endpoint for an eligible output/flow-input port first, then the target for an eligible input/flow-output port, treating an opposite-direction port as a direction failure.

witness.initial: A kept flow version has valid function nodes N and M. N declares only an input port named p, and M has no port named q. Its sole edge is from N.p to M.q.
events: The kernel proves it and reaches phase 3.
outcomes: An implementation that validates the source endpoint completely first reports that N.p has the wrong direction.
An implementation that first establishes existence of both named endpoints reports that M.q is missing before checking N.p's direction.
witness.observer: The composing agent sees a different first proof failure and reason.
